title: Getting Started with iAR
text: iAR package provides autoregressive models time series observed irregularly spaced time points, common situation astronomy, finance, environmental science. implements three complementary model classes: three share workflow: construct → simulate → estimate → forecast / interpolate.

title: Getting Started with iAR
text: Real astronomical environmental data rarely sampled regular grid. gentime() function generates realistic irregular time grids several distributions. first argument x defaults NULL, utilities object created internally can call gentime() directly without setup step. default distribution ("expmixture") mixes two exponential distributions, mimicking data sets observations closely spaced occasional long gaps occur. Alternative distributions include "uniform", "exponential", "gamma". Distribution inter-observation gaps (log scale) 100 irregular times drawn exponential mixture.
code:
set.seed(2847)  # x defaults to NULL — no setup needed times <- gentime(n = 100)@times  cat("Number of observations:", length(times), "
") #> Number of observations: 100 cat("Time span: [", round(min(times), 1), ",", round(max(times), 1), "]
") #> Time span: [ 162.8 , 3137.7 ] cat("Mean gap between observations:", round(mean(diff(times)), 2), "
") #> Mean gap between observations: 30.05 gaps <- diff(times) hist(log1p(gaps),      main = "Inter-observation gaps (log1p scale)",      xlab = "log(1 + gap)", col = "steelblue", border = "white",      breaks = 20)

title: Getting Started with iAR
text: Construct iAR object desired coefficient, call sim(). Simulated iAR series (phi = 0.9). irregular spacing visible unequal distances along x-axis.
code: set.seed(2847) times <- gentime(n = 100)@times  # Build the model: family = "norm", phi = 0.9 m_iar <- iAR(family = "norm", times = times, coef = 0.9) m_iar <- sim(m_iar)  head(m_iar@series) #> [1]  0.6949442  1.7577536  1.2249041  1.7570633  1.8224373 -1.6668806 plot(m_iar, type = "o",main = "Simulated iAR series (phi = 0.9)",ylab="Values",xlab="Time",pch=20)

title: Getting Started with iAR
text: Two estimators available: loglik() — direct MLE; supports three families ("norm", "t", "gamma"). kalman() — Kalman-filter MLE; available three model classes (iAR, CiAR, BiAR). estimation, standardise series (zero mean, unit variance) supply vector error standard deviations. simulated data measurement noise, zeros suffice.
code: y       <- m_iar@series y_std   <- y / sd(y)           # unit variance m_iar@series     <- y_std m_iar@series_esd <- rep(0, length(times))

title: Getting Started with iAR
text: CiAR extends iAR allow negative autocorrelation via complex coefficient ϕ=ϕR+iϕI\phi = \phi_R + \,\phi_I. stationarity condition |ϕ|=ϕR2+ϕI2<1|\phi| = \sqrt{\phi_R^2 + \phi_I^2} < 1.

title: Getting Started with iAR
code: set.seed(2847) times <- gentime(n = 100)@times  # phi = (0.9, 0): purely real CiAR — same as iAR but more general m_ciar <- CiAR(times = times, coef = c(0.9, 0)) m_ciar <- sim(m_ciar)  # Standardise y_c           <- m_ciar@series y_c_std       <- y_c / sd(y_c) m_ciar@series     <- y_c_std m_ciar@series_esd <- rep(0, length(times)) m_ciar <- kalman(m_ciar) cat("CiAR estimate: phiR =", round(m_ciar@coef[1], 4),     " phiI =", round(m_ciar@coef[2], 4), "\n") #> CiAR estimate: phiR = 0.9076  phiI = 0 cat("Modulus |phi| =", round(sqrt(sum(m_ciar@coef^2)), 4), "\n") #> Modulus |phi| = 0.9076

title: `BiAR` Class — BiAR
text: `BiAR` class designed handle bivariate irregularly observed time series data using autoregressive approach. extends `multidata` class include additional properties modeling bivariate time series. Key features `BiAR` class include: - Support bivariate time series data. - Forecasting interpolation functionalities irregular time points. - Assumptions zero-mean standardized processes, configurable user. - Estimation model parameters likelihoods, including Kalman likelihood.

title: `BiAR` Class — BiAR
text: - `@times` must numeric vector without dimensions strictly increasing. - `@series` must numeric matrix two columns (bivariate) empty. - number rows `@series` must match length `@times`. - `@series_esd`, provided, must numeric matrix. dimensions must match `@series`, must one row number columns. - `@series_esd` contains NA values, must correspond positionally NA values `@series`. - `@series_names`, provided, must character vector length equal number columns `@series`, names must unique. - `@coef` must numeric vector length 2, element strictly -1 1. - modulus `sqrt(phiR^2 + phiI^2)` must strictly less 1 (stationarity condition). - `@tAhead` must strictly positive numeric scalar.
